name: Lexicon LXP-5
source: Lexicon LXP-5 Owner's Manual, Part #070-07332 Rev 1 (c) 1989/1995, 69 pp. (freeverb3-vst.sourceforge.io/doc/Lexicon/lxp5.pdf = the manualslib 382517 'Rev 1' manual; text layer, read directly): front panel p.1-2, rear panel (MIDI OUT/THRU slide switch) p.1-3, LEARN LED p.2-3, presets p.2-4..2-6, user memory + factory user banks 5-8 pp.2-7..2-10, algorithms + block diagrams p.2-11, Edit A/B tables pp.2-13..2-14, ADJUST destination p.2-18, store/write-protect p.2-19, algorithm change p.2-21, footswitch pp.2-22..2-23, MIDI channel learn / program change / LEARN+PC store pp.3-1..3-3, patches + Edit C + MIDI learn + clock as source pp.3-4..3-13, MIDI Implementation Data ch.4 pp.4-1..4-14 (Data Requests, Event Requests, Active Setup, Stored Program, Parameter Adjust, All User Data, dump contents, parameter map, patch sources, microcode map + ranges, implementation chart). Family cross-checks: PCM 70 Owner's Manual v3.00 p.6-4 (same Lexicon ID 06 framing, status nibble 0 active / 1 stored / 2 param, requests 3n with 60h/61h -- but PCM70 data is nybblized, 10-bit params); LXP-1 Owner's Manual pp.4-6..4-14 (16-bit packed values, NOT byte-compatible). Open-source senders: philipkent/lxp5editor (Python, send-only: F0 06 05 2n pp vv F7 for params 0-22 and 44-62), evenbrenden/lxpx (Pd, LXP-1 packing). Electra One 'LXP-5' preset by oldgearguy (forum.electra.one/t/lexicon-lxp-5/2909): reads dumps, checks the sumcheck, mentions undocumented messages for selecting user/factory programs -- details unpublished. MidiQuest lists LXP-5 Patch + Patch Bank. Lexicon MRC manual not found online.

lexicon.statusByte: Byte 3 = (type << 4) | n, n = MIDI channel 0-15 (the unit's one channel; no OMNI). type: 0 = Active Setup data, 1 = Stored (single program) data, 2 = Parameter Adjust, 3 = Data Request, 4 = All User data, 6 = Event Request. SysEx on another channel is ignored.

formats.dataRequest:
F0 06 05 3n

F7 (7 bytes). e = 60h active setup (p ignored), 61h one register (p = register 0-127), 62h one parameter (p = param #), 64h all registers (p ignored). Byte 5 must be present even when ignored.
formats.activeSetupData: F0 06 05 0n 5E <94 data bytes> <sumcheck> F7 = 101 bytes. 5E = byte count 94. Data byte i = parameter i-1 (byte 0 = algorithm ID, byte 67 repeats it); includes knob-mechanism params 23-30, memory location 64, preset # 65 and the system params 67-92. The edit buffer as it is running.
formats.storedProgramData: F0 06 05 1n <reg 0-127> 39 <57 data bytes> <sumcheck> F7 = 65 bytes. 39 = byte count 57. Layout: byte 0 = algorithm (param 66), 1-23 = params 0-22, 24-34 = name (31-41), 35 = reserved (42), 36 = ADJUST destination (43), 37-56 = patches 1-4 (44-63), i.e. byte = param + 1 for 0-22, param - 7 for 31-63.
formats.parameterAdjust: F0 06 05 2n <param 0-127> <value 0-127> F7 (7 bytes). Sets the edit buffer (base value) immediately; no reply. Also what the unit transmits on knob moves.
formats.allUserData: F0 06 05 4n 39 00 <7296 data bytes> <sumcheck> F7 = 7304 bytes. 39 00 = byte count 7296 (0x1C80) as two 7-bit bytes, high first. 128 x the 57-byte stored program, register 0 first (order inferred from the LXP-1 manual; LXP-5 manual only says 'all 128 copies').
formats.eventRequest: F0 06 05 6n <e> <reg 0-127> F7 (7 bytes). e = 70h store the edit buffer into register reg; 71h recall register reg into the edit buffer. No reply documented (the LEARN LED blinks green/red for ~2 s on a store).
formats.sumcheck: 'sumcheck of data bytes', algorithm not given. Candidates: sum(data) & 7F, or (-sum(data)) & 7F. Decide on the first real dump: compute both, keep the one that matches (store it in prefs 'sumcheck'). Until then accept dumps whose sumcheck fails but flag them.
formats.noNybbles: All data is 7-bit, one byte per parameter (MSB always 0). No nybbles, no packing (unlike PCM70 / LXP-1).

lexicon.encoding: raw 7-bit, one byte per parameter. Unipolar 0-127; bipolar (patch scale, and per p.4-9 possibly pitch adjust) = 7-bit two's complement (-64..+63).
lexicon.programNumbering: User registers 0-127 = USER bank floor(r / 16) + 1 (1-8), SELECT position r % 16 (MIN, 2..15, MAX) = 'location' r + 1 (1-128). Presets 0-63 = FUNCTION PITCH / DELAY / CHORUS / MULTI (floor(p / 16)), SELECT position p % 16 = preset # p + 1 (1-64).
lexicon.transmits: Only with the rear OUT/THRU slide switch at OUT. Parameter Adjust (2n pp vv) when (a) the ADJUST knob is turned in play mode -- pp = the param ADJUST drives, (b) a parameter is changed in Edit mode, (c) a program is recalled with the FUNCTION/SELECT knobs ('the appropriate program parameter change message', presumably param 64 or 65 -- unverified). Transmitted values = base + MIDI patch offset (received values set the base). Replies to 3n requests. Never Program Change, CC or clock (implementation chart).
lexicon.receives: Program Change 0-127 (loads a program; see programs), CC 0-31 + switches + notes/velocity/aftertouch/pitch bend/MIDI clock only as patch sources, System Reset. SysEx: all of the above messages (active setup, stored data, parameter adjust, all user data, requests, events).
lexicon.midiClock: Received, but only as a patch SOURCE ('MIDI tempo period', source 68): a patch from clock to a delay param makes tempo-synced delays (delay time ignores the base value; halved until it fits). No tap tempo, no clock-synced LFO, no clock out. Factory user programs 81-83, 100, 101 need clock.
lexicon.sharedWith: Not the same byte format as any other unit in the rack. Lexicon family resemblance only: the PCM 70 (v3.00) uses the same F0 06 <model> <type|chan> framing and 60h/61h request codes but nybblized data + 10-bit params; the LXP-1 uses 16-bit values packed 7-into-8. The LXP-15 manual was not checked.

groups.name: Delays 1-3 coarse/fine + feedback 1-2 (Delay 3 + Feedback 2: Pitch/Delay only)
Pitch shifter (Pitch/Delay only): base octave, interval, fine adjust
Reverb / ambience: decay, treble decay, bass multiply, size, diffusion
Levels: reverb balance, output balance, output/input level, LFO rate
General purpose (Dynamic MIDI) patches 1-4: source, threshold, destination, scale, offset
System (not stored with programs): footswitch, write protect, global patch enable
Global patch sources for microcode params 0-22 (system; factory CC 8-30, shipped disabled)

params.name: Algorithm
params.note: Program (algorithm) ID: 1 = Delay/Reverb, 2 = Pitch/Delay, 3 = Bypass (manual p.4-7). Byte 0 of every dump (and byte 67 of the active setup). Edit B / SELECT 14 on the panel. Changing it re-interprets every microcode value below (ranges differ per algorithm).

params.name: Delay 1 Coarse
params.note: Mono delay (P/D: before the pitch shifter; D/R: the modulated delay). P/D 0-1.0404 s, D/R 0-630.8 ms, ~8.2 ms/step (128 / 78 steps). Max is 77 in Delay/Reverb.

params.name: Delay 1 Fine
params.note: Added to Delay 1 Coarse: 0-8.1 ms in 64 us steps (p.4-10). The Edit A table says 0-61.5 ms -- see uncertain.

params.name: Feedback 1
params.note: 0-100% (~0.79%/step). P/D: 100% cuts the input = loop sampler; D/R: 100% keeps adding input.

params.name: Delay 2 Coarse
params.note: P/D: right channel + reverb pre-delay, 0-322.5 ms; D/R: reverb pre-delay, 0-176.6 ms; 2.56 ms/step. Max 126 (P/D) / 69 (D/R).

params.name: Delay 2 Fine
params.note: Added to Delay 2 Coarse: 0-2.5 ms, ~20 us/step.

params.name: Feedback 2
params.note: Pitch/Delay only: feedback around the pitch shifter + left delay, 0-99%. N/A in Delay/Reverb.

params.name: Delay 3 Coarse
params.note: Pitch/Delay only: left channel delay 0-322.5 ms, 2.56 ms/step.

params.name: Delay 3 Fine
params.note: Pitch/Delay only: added to Delay 3 Coarse, 0-2.5 ms.

params.name: Pitch Base/Select
params.note: Pitch/Delay only. Base octave that Pitch Interval adds to; 0 removes the shifter (and its delay). Manual: over MIDI use 1 (down 2 oct) + Interval 0-36 for the whole range.

params.name: Pitch Interval
params.note: Pitch/Delay only. Semitones up from the base: with base = down 2 oct, 0-36 = -24 st .. +12 st (actually maj 7th + 47 cents at the top). The shifter may not cross unison cleanly.

params.name: Pitch Adjust
params.note: Pitch/Delay only. Fine detune, -64..+63 arbitrary units (~4 cents/step at +1 oct, ~25 cents/step at -2 oct). p.4-11: 'the MIDI value 0-127 is interpreted as being centered on 64' -- modelled as offset binary (raw 64 = 0). p.4-9's general rule says bipolar = two's complement: see uncertain.

params.name: Decay Time
params.note: Mid reverb time. P/D 0.5-12 s (15 steps, max 14); D/R 0.5 s - infinite (16 steps; 15 = infinite, min 0.1 s). Step values are not linear and not published.

params.name: Treble Decay
params.note: Low-pass inside the reverb: 320 Hz .. full range (15 = flat), logarithmic, 16 steps.

params.name: Bass Multiply
params.note: Bass reverb time x0.3 .. x2.5, linear, 32 steps. x1.0 = ADJUST position 9 on the panel; the raw value for x1.0 is not printed (linear interpolation gives ~10).

params.name: Size
params.note: Room side length: P/D 8-26 m (26 steps, max 25); D/R 8-53.5 m (64 steps). Changing it mutes the unit briefly.

params.name: Diffusion
params.note: 0-100% in 1% steps (101 steps).

params.name: High Cut Filter
params.note: 320 Hz .. full range (15 = flat), logarithmic, 16 steps.

params.name: Low Cut Filter
params.note: Full range (0 = flat) .. 1350 Hz, logarithmic, 32 steps.

params.name: Reverb Balance
params.note: 0 = 100% effects / 0% reverb .. 127 = 0% effects / 100% reverb; sine/cosine pan law (-3 dB at centre).

params.name: Output Balance
params.note: Wet output pan: 0 = 100% left .. 127 = 100% right, sine/cosine law.

params.name: Output Level
params.note: 0-100% (includes +6 dB make-up; ~70% gives smoother pans).

params.name: Input Level
params.note: DSP input level 0-100% (not the front-panel INPUT pot). Patching a pedal here gates loops/infinite reverb.

params.name: LFO Rate
params.note: 0.066-10 Hz log approximation (p.4-13); the Edit B table and p.3-12 say 0.066-5 Hz. Only audible through a patch whose source is the LFO.

params.name: ADJUST Knob Destination
params.note: Microcode param # 0-22 the front-panel ADJUST knob drives (stored per program). Edit B / SELECT 13 offers only 16 of the 23 (no fines, pitch base/adjust, bass multiply, diffusion). The manual says up to five params can follow ADJUST -- the extra ones are presumably general-purpose patches with source 69 (ADJUST knob).

params.name: Patch 1 Source
params.note: Control source 0-127: 0-31 = CC 0-31, 32-63 = switches 0-31, 64 last note, 65 velocity, 66 channel aftertouch, 67 pitch bend, 68 MIDI tempo period (clock), 69 ADJUST knob, 70 LFO, 71 lowest note, 72 highest note (p.4-8). 73-127 undefined. How 'patch off' is encoded is not stated (Edit C offers 'Patch Off'); the Edit C source list uses Mod Wheel / Breath / Foot / Data Entry / Volume = CC 1/2/4/6/7 and Sustain = a switch (assumed switch 0 = CC 64).

params.name: Patch 1 Threshold
params.note: 0-127 (Edit C offers 16 steps). Offset = (Source - Threshold) x Scale.

params.name: Patch 1 Destination
params.note: Microcode param # 0-22.

params.name: Patch 1 Scale Factor
params.note: Signed scale, 7-bit two's complement on the wire (-64..+63; manual prints '-64 to +64'). Edit C steps: x-2.0 -1.0 -0.8 -0.6 -0.4 -0.3 -0.2 -0.1 +0.1 +0.2 +0.3 +0.4 +0.6 +0.8 +1.0 +2.0 -- raw-value <-> multiplier mapping not published. For a clock (68) source the MIDI LEARN scale selects a note duration (half .. 32nd, p.3-13).

params.name: Patch 1 Offset
params.note: Last calculated offset ((source - threshold) x scale), recomputed continuously by the unit and stored with the program so the destination holds its value until the controller moves. Writing it is pointless (overwritten 'shortly thereafter'); read it to see the patch contribution. Encoding (signed?) not stated.

params.name: Footswitch Mode
params.note: 0 (and 4-127) = Defeat Input, 1 = Defeat Output, 2 = Bypass, 3 = Memory Increment. Not stored per program. Edit B / SELECT 15.

params.name: Memory Write Protect
params.note: Nonzero = all 128 user registers write protected (stores fail, LEARN LED flashes red). Edit B / SELECT MAX.

params.name: Global Patch Enable
params.note: 0 = global patches off (factory state), 1 = ignored on setup recall until the source moves, 2 = active immediately on recall. Edit A / SELECT MAX (MIN-6 / 7-11 / 12-MAX).

systemParams.name: Delay 0 Coarse Edit Knob
systemParams.note: knob mechanism (front-panel coarse/fine delay editing); active setup only, not stored

systemParams.name: Reserved
systemParams.note: byte 35 of a stored program: carry through from the mirror

systemParams.name: Preset #
systemParams.note: 0-63 = preset table, 64 = Bypass, 65 = edit buffer, 127 = memory location (then 64 says which). Not stored. Likely the SysEx way to select a factory preset (2n 41 pp) -- unverified.

1.name: Delay/Reverb
1.chain: Input -> EQ -> Delay 1 (modulated, Feedback 1) -> Delay 2 (pre-delay) -> diffusor -> reverb -> Reverb Balance -> L/R

2.name: Pitch/Delay
2.chain: Input -> Delay 1 (Feedback 1) -> pitch shifter -> EQ -> Delay 2 (R) / Delay 3 (L) (Feedback 2 around shifter + left) -> ambience -> Reverb Balance -> L/R
2.presets: all PITCH, DELAY, CHORUS and MULTI 49-56

editA: 10 Pitch Interval (0-15 st up from base)
frontPanel.learn: Hold LEARN + turn FUNCTION to EDIT A/B/C = enter edit; hold LEARN + FUNCTION to USER n/SELECT = store; hold LEARN + send a MIDI message = set channel; hold LEARN + send PC = store to register PC; hold LEARN + move a controller (+ ADJUST for scale) = MIDI-learn patch 1.
frontPanel.notMidi: INPUT, MIX and OUTPUT pots are analogue and not stored or reported.

banks.label: user
banks.note:
Registers 0-127 (USER 1-8 x 16). Program Change p loads register p (inferred: 128 PCs, 128 registers, and LEARN + PC p stores to register p; the manual never says PC reaches the 64 presets). Read without selecting: 3n 61

-> 1n

39 <57> ck. Store: load the edit buffer (2n param stream, or a 0n active-setup dump -- unverified as receivable), then 6n 70

; or send a 1n

stored dump (unverified as writing the register). Write protect (param 68) must be off.

banks.label: presets
banks.note:
ROM presets 1-64 (PITCH/DELAY/CHORUS/MULTI x 16). Not readable as stored data. Selection over MIDI is UNVERIFIED: try 2n 41

(param 65 = Preset #), then 3n 60 to read the edit buffer. Factory user registers 1-64 are copies of these, so PC 0-63 reaches the same sounds on a unit that still has its factory user memory.

ccMap.note: There is no fixed CC map. CCs only act through patches: (a) the four per-program general purpose patches (any CC 0-31 or switch as source), (b) the 23 global patches, whose factory sources are CC 8-30 -> microcode params 0-22 (CC 8 = Delay 1 Coarse ... CC 30 = LFO Rate) but which ship DISABLED (param 69 = 0). With global enable = 2 the factory map is a ready-made live CC surface; the sources are re-assignable only by SysEx (params 70-92).

areas.what: edit buffer + system params (globals, write protect, footswitch)

backup.restore: Write protect off (Edit B / SELECT MAX at MIN-8, or 2n 44 00). Send the 7304-byte 4n All User dump back -- UNVERIFIED that the unit accepts it (manual: 'identical whether transmitted ... or received as a Data Dump'); verify by re-reading 64h and comparing. Fallback per register: 1n <r> dump, or edit-buffer load + 6n 70 <r>, 30 ms+ apart. System params 67-92 restore as 2n param adjusts from the active-setup dump.
backup.notInSysex: Front-panel INPUT/MIX/OUTPUT pots, the rear MIDI OUT/THRU switch, the MIDI channel (set only by LEARN), the footswitch state.

setup: Rear panel: slide the recessed MIDI switch to OUT (it is one jack, OUT or THRU). At THRU the LXP-5 transmits nothing and every read times out.
Cable both ways: interface out -> LXP-5 MIDI IN, LXP-5 MIDI OUT -> interface in.

MIDI channel (no OMNI, no channel display): hold LEARN and send any complete channel message on the editor's channel (a note, or a pitch bend -- not a program change, and not under running status), release LEARN. The unit now answers on that channel; SysEx carries the channel in byte 3 and must match.
Do not hold LEARN while the editor sends program changes: LEARN + PC stores the edit buffer into that register (and LEARN also re-learns the channel from the PC).
To store from the editor: Memory Write Protect off (FUNCTION EDIT B, SELECT MAX, ADJUST to MIN-8; or the editor sends param 68 = 0). Stores into presets are refused (LEARN LED flashes red).
Leave FUNCTION on a USER position (not a PRESET or EDIT position) while the editor works; turning FUNCTION/SELECT on the panel recalls a program and overrides edits.
No MIDI clock needed unless a program patches 'MIDI tempo period'; if one does, stop clock while MIDI-learning patches (clock wins the learn).
Battery: if user programs come back as garbage names/values, the memory battery is dead -- back up before replacing it.
uncertain: Sumcheck algorithm: the manual only says 'sumcheck of data bytes'. The Electra One preset author verifies it on real dumps but did not publish the formula. Test both (sum & 7F) and (-sum & 7F) against the first dump.

Param-data request (3n 62 pp): reply format not documented -- most likely a Parameter Adjust message (2n pp vv) carrying base + patch offset. The request table also mentions 'e = 65' which is not in the code list: ignore.

Receiving dumps: p.4-2 says data is 'identical in format whether transmitted ... or received as a Data Dump', but whether a received 0n active setup loads the edit buffer, a received 1n stored dump writes register p, and a received 4n dump rewrites all registers (honouring write protect?) is not stated. Verify each on hardware before relying on it for sendPatch/store/restore.
Event requests (6n 70 / 71): no acknowledgement is documented. Treat a store as unconfirmed until a 61h read-back of that register matches.

Program Change map: PC 0-127 assumed = user registers 1-128 (consistent with LEARN + PC store and 128 PCs; Cakewalk/Ardour .midnam names PC 0-63 with the preset names, which matches the factory copy in registers 1-64). How (or whether) a PC reaches the ROM presets is not documented; the Electra One author reports 'undocumented MIDI messages that made selecting user and factory patches much more reliable'. Candidate: param 65 (Preset #) via 2n 41 pp. Capture what the unit sends when FUNCTION/SELECT recalls a preset vs a register.

What the unit transmits when a program is recalled from the panel ('the appropriate program parameter change message'): probably param 64 (memory location) or 65 (preset #). Capture it during the mapping session; decode() should then follow panel program changes.

Pitch Adjust encoding: p.4-11 says the 0-127 value is 'centered on 64' (offset binary, modelled), p.4-9 says bipolar params use two's complement. The python lxp5editor sends two's complement. Test: send 2n 0A 40 and 2n 0A 00 on a pitched program and listen for which one is 'no detune'.
Patch scale factor raw <-> multiplier mapping (Edit C offers x-2.0 .. x+2.0 in 16 steps) and how 'Patch Off' is stored are not printed. Patch offset encoding unknown.

Range disagreements between the Edit A/B tables (front panel) and the MIDI chapter: Delay 1 Coarse 0-983 ms vs 0-1.0404 s (P/D), Delay 1 Fine 0-61.5 ms vs 0-8.1 ms, Delay 2/3 Coarse 0-307.2 ms vs 0-322.5 ms, Delay 2 Fine 0-19.2 ms vs 0-2.5 ms, LFO 0.066-5 Hz vs 10 Hz, Algorithm select ADJUST zones MIN-6/7-11/12-MAX (p.2-14) vs MIN-5/6-10/11-MAX (p.2-21). The MIDI-chapter values are used for the microcode params; the front-panel figures probably describe the knob-mechanism params 23-30.
Decay Time, Treble Decay, Hi/Lo Cut and Size step tables are not published (only end points), so displays stay raw integers.
Out-of-range values: what the unit does with e.g. Delay 1 Coarse > 77 in Delay/Reverb is not stated. The editor should clamp to the current algorithm's range (params[].ranges).
MIDI clock: the implementation chart marks clock as recognized 'used as controller'; everything about tempo sync is via patch source 68. No evidence of clock-synced LFO or tap tempo.
Name character set (params 31-41) and padding not documented.
All-user dump order (register 0 first) is taken from the LXP-1 manual; the LXP-5 manual does not say.
Pacing: no figure for the LXP-5. 30 ms between messages follows the PCM 70 note ('requires 30 ms between stored bulk data messages'); a 7304-byte dump takes ~2.3 s on the wire.
driverNotes:
Lexicon LXP-5 (Lexicon 06h, model 05h). Every message is F0 06 05 <(type << 4) | n> ... F7 with n = channel() (learned on the unit with LEARN; no OMNI, no device ID). Match incoming on F0 06 05 and the type nibble; adopt the channel nibble if it differs. (1) DATA: a stored program is 57 raw 7-bit bytes, one per parameter -- p.offset (byte 0 = algorithm, 1-23 = params 0-22, 24-56 = params 31-63); the active setup is 94 bytes with byte = p.setupOffset = pnum + 1 (byte 0 also = algorithm). No nybbles. Keep the last 57-byte program mirror and carry byte 35 (reserved param 42) and the patch offsets (readOnly) through untouched. Signed params (encoding 'twos7'): wire = v & 7F, read = b >= 64 ? b - 128 : b. pitchAdjust: offset binary (valueOffset -64) until the uncertain test says otherwise. Sumcheck: see lexicon.formats.sumcheck -- learn which formula on the first dump, store it in prefs 'sumcheck', and compute it for every dump sent. (2) READ: requestPatch = send F0 06 05 3n 60 00 F7, wait up to ~500 ms for F0 06 05 0n 5E <94> ck F7 (101 bytes); values from setupOffset; also refresh the system params (67-92) from it. requestProgram(0, r) = send 3n 61 , wait for 1n 39 <57> ck F7 (65 bytes, match on byte 4 = r) -- reads a register without changing what plays (bank 'user' dump:true). Presets cannot be read (dump:false): select + requestPatch. (3) EDIT: sendParam(p, v) = F0 06 05 2n F7. Coalesce to the newest value per param, >= 30 ms apart (gapMs). Clamp microcode values to p.ranges[current algorithm] (null = the param does not exist in that algorithm: do not send). Size changes mute the unit briefly: throttle harder (~150 ms). sendPatch(values) = until a received 0n dump is proven to load the edit buffer, stream all program params as 2n messages (algorithm FIRST, then microcode 0-22, name 31-41, 43, patches 44-62; skip offsets 48/53/58/63) -- ~56 x 7 bytes. (4) programChange(0, r) = C0|n, r (user registers). Presets (bank 1): the select is unverified -- try F0 06 05 2n 41

F7 (param 65 = Preset #) and confirm by reading 60h; if it fails, mark presets as not selectable. After any program change, requestPatch to adopt the sound. (5) writeProgram(0, r, values): refuse if writeProtect != 0 (send 2n 44 00 only if the user asked); load the edit buffer (sendPatch), wait ~100 ms, send F0 06 05 6n 70 F7, wait ~300 ms, then verify with requestProgram(0, r) + sameProgram. No ack exists, so the read-back IS the confirmation; a mismatch = write protect on / wrong channel. Return the 57 bytes. (6) probe: send 3n 60 00 F7 on the saved channel, wait 400 ms for an 0n reply. If none, sweep n = 0..15 (one request each, ~150 ms) and keep the first that answers (prefs 'ch' via the editor's channel). No reply at all = rear switch at THRU or MIDI OUT not cabled. (7) sameProgram(a, b): compare the 57-byte programs except the patch offsets (bytes 41, 46, 51, 56) and reserved byte 35. (8) decode(ev): unsolicited F0 06 05 2n pp vv F7 = a panel edit or ADJUST move -> [{param: byPnum(pp), value: read(vv)}] -- the value includes any patch offset (base + offset), so a param under an active patch will jitter; pp 64/65 (program recalled on the panel) -> trigger the editor's follow logic (re-read 60h). Ignore 2n for pnums not in params (knob mechanism 23-30). Also accept unsolicited 0n/1n dumps (another unit or the MRC). (9) PACING: 30 ms between short messages, >= 100 ms after any dump, one outstanding request at a time. Bank backup: one 3n 64 00 F7 -> 7304 bytes (~2.4 s; wait up to 5 s), split into 128 x 57 by register; fallback 128 x 61h. (10) MAPPING SESSION (first time on the hardware, before trusting any unverified path): a) probe + 60h read, check the sumcheck formula; b) for each microcode param: 2n pp v, read 60h, confirm byte pp+1 == v and listen; c) 62h pp read and log the reply format; d) turn ADJUST and each FUNCTION/SELECT position, log what arrives; e) try 2n 41 for preset select; f) send a 1n dump to a scratch register and read it back; g) 6n 70/71 round-trip; h) 64h dump, then send it back to a cleared copy and re-read (only after a saved backup). Record results in this schema's uncertain list.
